cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration: by building an in-house brass manufacturing, forging and extrusion facility at Noida Facility 1, the Company states it has integrated backward to ensure quality and supply control. It manufactures brass billets and rods using brass alloys primarily comprising copper and zinc, which are further processed into forged components, extruded sections and brass machining parts in accordance with customer specifications; the forged and extruded products are then subjected to machining operations such as turning, drilling, tapping and threading to achieve required dimensions and tolerances. Through this integrated process the Company converts brass into forging parts and machined components within its own manufacturing facilities and manages raw material processing and component production internally. Inputs: primary raw materials are brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, copper rods, aluminium rods and consumables such as zinc ingots, flux and oil, procured from domestic and international suppliers on a purchase order basis; the risk factors also list steel round bar and aluminium solid rod. During Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 raw materials were imported from 7 countries - South Korea, Vietnam, Thailand, China, Japan, Italy and the United Kingdom. Domestic purchases were 90.29% (Fiscal 2026), 74.74% (Fiscal 2025) and 54.82% (Fiscal 2024) of purchases, with import purchases at 9.71%, 25.26% and 45.18% respectively. The Company usually does not enter into long-term supply contracts with raw material suppliers; pricing and production volumes are negotiated for each purchase order. High-precision machinery (automatic tube cutting machine, integrated CNC bending machine, automatic forming machine, automatic brazing machine, linear 5-axis brazing machine, transfer machining centre, forging machine, packing line, brass melting furnace, brass extrusion press, forging press) is sourced from domestic and international machinery manufacturers in China and South Korea. Outbound, finished goods are transported by road, sea and air on CIF or FOB terms through third-party transportation and logistics providers. Facilities are spread across five strategically located sites in India at Noida, Neemrana, Pune, Bengaluru and Sanand covering a total area of 32,351.84 square meters, and inventory is managed through Sofgen, an ERP system.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Revenue from the top 5 customers was Rs. 39,338.26 lakhs, Rs. 30,769.74 lakhs and Rs. 22,746.95 lakhs, being 84.09%, 79.15% and 75.45% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the top 10 contributed 96.60%, 96.02% and 92.01%. The DRHP states the loss of any of these customers could have a material adverse effect on business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
- White goods (HVAC & Refrigerator) accounted for 93.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, up from 87.79% in Fiscal 2025 and 88.11% in Fiscal 2024, leaving results tied to a single demand cycle.
- Primary raw materials are brass scrap, brass honey scrap, copper tubes, copper rods, aluminium rods and steel round bar, plus consumables such as zinc ingots, flux and oil, procured from both domestic and international suppliers on a purchase order basis rather than under committed long-term supply.
- Revenue from operations grew from Rs. 30,170.42 lakhs in Fiscal 2024 to Rs. 46,808.59 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.50% in Fiscal 2026 from 10.08% in Fiscal 2025, PBT margin to 5.20% from 7.11% and PAT margin to 3.75% from 5.26%.
- Fiscal 2025 Restated Financial Statements are consolidated following Sai Ganesh Exports Private Limited becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary, while Fiscals 2026 and 2024 are standalone; Sai Ganesh Exports Private Limited was amalgamated with the Company in Fiscal 2026.
- The fund requirements and deployment for the Sanand expansion and the new Sri City, Andhra Pradesh facility are based on internal management estimates and have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution, and no commissioning timeline is disclosed.
- Industry and market data are derived from the D&B Report titled 'Industry Report on Tubing Components and Fittings Industry' dated July 3, 2026, exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company; the DRHP itself carries a risk factor on reliance on such information.
- The four Promoters - Jignesh Panchal, Dina Panchal, Jugal Jignesh Panchal and Jubin Jignesh Panchal - hold 1,57,87,255 Equity Shares, being 99.99% of the pre-issue paid-up Equity Share capital, and three of the eight Board seats (Chairman and Managing Director plus two Whole-time Directors) are held by Promoters.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Fund the capital expenditure requirements towards setting up a new manufacturing facility at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh from the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue.**
- **Repay and/or pre-pay, in full or in part, borrowings availed by the Company using the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue.**
- **Complete a Fresh Issue of up to 49,20,000 Equity Shares of face value Rs. 10 each together with an offer for sale of up to 2,60,000 Equity Shares by the Promoter Selling Shareholder.**
- **Apply a portion of the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue towards general corporate purposes.**
- **Continue operating the in-house brass manufacturing, forging and extrusion facility at Noida Facility 1 to convert brass into forged parts and machined components internally and manage raw material processing in-house.**
- **Pursue grant of four patent applications filed jointly with Promoter Jignesh Panchal before the Indian Patent Office covering stainless steel-copper muffler/accumulator, header assembly, evaporator out assembly and suction tube products, …**
- **Sustain product development through the New Product Development and Industrialisation team of 17 employees housed at the Manufacturing Facilities.**
- **Manufacturing Capacity stood at 6,91,20,000 Nos. in Fiscal 2026, up from 5,39,40,000 Nos. in Fiscal 2025 and 3,83,43,000 Nos. in Fiscal 2024 - the base against which the Sanand and Sri City additions can be tracked.**
- **Maintain the repeat-customer base, which stood at 19 repeat customers contributing 95.30% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 (95.18% in Fiscal 2025 and 88.59% in Fiscal 2024).**
- **Management explicitly flags that the loss of any of the top 5 or top 10 customers, which contributed 84.09% and 96.60% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, could have a material adverse effect on the business.**
- **Extend the manufacturing footprint beyond the existing five sites at Noida, Neemrana, Pune, Bengaluru and Sanand covering 32,351.84 square meters, by expanding Sanand and adding Sri City, Andhra Pradesh.**
